english.title: Cause / allow the death of a child / vulnerable adult
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a member of the same household as and having had frequent contact with a person who was at that time a

(A)_[child,]_
(B)_[vulnerable adult,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THE NAME..), you caused that person's death or were, or ought to have been, aware that there was a significant risk of serious physical harm being caused to that person by the unlawful act of a member of

(C)_[his]_
(D)_[her]_

household which occurred in circumstances of the kind that you foresaw or ought to have foreseen and you failed to take such steps as you could reasonably have been expected to take to protect

(E)_[him]_
(F)_[her]_

from that risk
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(1) and (7) of the Domestic Violence, Crime and Victims Act 2004

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) On the 28th June 2022, the penalty for offences under this section was increased on indictment from a maximum of 14 years imprisonment to life imprisonment by section 123 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022. For the offence applying from that date, see H100755.
(ii) Section 5(2) provides that prosecution does not have to prove whether it was the defendant who committed the act or the person who failed to take steps to prevent it
(iii) Section 5(3)(a) provides that if the accused was not the mother or father of the deceased then they MAY NOT be charged with this offence if they were under the age of 16 at the time of the act that caused the death and section 5(3)(b) provides that for the purposes of subsection (1)(d)(ii) they could not have been expected to take any such step as is referred to there before attaining that age.
